title: Catalan's constant is irrational
main_claim: G = beta(2) is irrational. The proof uses determinants Delta_N of size 48N built from mixed moments, whose Chebyshev rows have Taylor contact that cancels zeta(2). If G were rational, the product formula plus p-adic denominator bounds would give liminf(log|Delta_N|/n^2 - log2/2) > -2.29084 along N = p prime, where nonvanishing comes from a Frobenius reduction to three fixed 48x48 matrices certified mod 101. An Andreief/Cauchy integral representation, a Hardy-space interpolation bound or a Hadamard bound, and a Chebyshev-expansion energy dual with explicit rational trial sequences give limsup <= -2.290939875. The two bounds contradict each other.

issues.location: Sec. 6-7 (energy reduction, certificate) vs Prop. 3.x finite-place bound
issues.description: Not a gap: the contradiction rests on a very small numerical margin. The true constants are about -2.29110 (real-place, kappa=2, using the exact trial sequences) and -2.29081 (finite-place), a difference of about 3e-4. So any O(1e-4) slip in either constant would break the proof. Every constant I recomputed agrees, but the root-exhaustion polynomial certificate (Descartes counts and bracket signs) was not recomputed polynomial by polynomial; I located the suprema with a dense grid instead.

coverage: Read all sections in full. Checked by hand: the sheet coefficients (1/2,1/2) and (-1/4,5/4); the Blaschke/Cauchy-gluing interpolation lemma and the H^2 determinant cancellation; Hadamard weights; the exact energy identity (all log2, |x|, log(1+x^2), log(1-x) exponents and the constant -33/48); the damping comparisons and diagonal corrections; the direction of the lambda*D term; the 2-adic quadratic minimization (505/4608); the R/S tables, loss function d(x) and its integral 8609/2; the central-layer lemma and the integral column elimination. Computational checks: (1) moment decomposition M = M0 + 4G c + 1.5 zeta(2) c against 2D quadrature; (2) exact zeta(2) cancellation in every raw entry for N=1, 2; (3) digit-reduction lemma exactly for N=1, all primes 17..61 and all i,j<65 (50,700 cases, 0 failures); (4) exact rational Delta_1 and Delta_2 for several test G values: v_p(Delta_N) >= -bound for every prime above 2*sqrt(H), with equality at many primes; (5) the mod-101 Gaussian pivots and swaps for B0, B0+B1, B0-B1, which match the paper's table exactly, plus nonzero rational determinants and auxiliary-row degrees 18/19; (6) the Frobenius identities (P-identity and D-identity) mod p for p=3,5,7; (7) the certificate suprema and norms with mpmath from the exact trial sequences; (8) a 4000-digit numerical Delta_1, giving -2.2356 at N=1, consistent with finite-size corrections. Not independently verified: the 2-adic bound beyond its algebra (it is asymptotic); the Descartes and bracket polynomial certificate (replaced by grid suprema); the uniform-in-N argument for the digit lemma beyond N=1, 2.
